title: answer_approval input
description: Records the signed-in person's own answer to an approval request they were asked: approve or reject, with a typed reason to reject and where the approval rule asks for one. Served only to a person in the product's web app (D-38); an AI client is never served it, because AI never approves. The token proves who answered: the input names no responder. The engine checks that the person holds the role, or the owner role on the decision's application, that the request asks for, now; that no separation rule keeps the answer from counting; that the person's approval does not already count for the same requirement; and that the request is still pending and not expired. It then counts the answer as it counts an answer from a card, and accepts or rejects the decision when the rule is met. A refused answer writes nothing.

approvalRecordId.description: The approval request to answer, from get_approval_status or the decision page.

answer.description: approve or reject. A consultation answer is recorded and shown, and never counts.

reason.description: The typed reason. Required to reject, and to approve where the approval rule asks for one (document 26, AN-08). Stored on the approval record as the person typed it.

validateOnly.description: True runs every check and the recompute and returns what would be written, without writing. The decision page can use it to show the buttons only to a person who may answer.

examples.reason: The data use goes beyond what the privacy notice covers.
